Title: Login page renders branding and both fields
Steps:
1. Go to /
2. Wait for the form
Expected Result: Heading 'Sign in' visible. 'Civilytics' and 'Satyaki Solutions Pvt Ltd' visible. Username and Password fields visible. Sign in button visible.
Playwright Selector Hints:
getByRole('heading',{name:'Sign in'})
getByText('Civilytics')
getByLabel('Username')
getByLabel('Password')
getByRole('button',{name:'Sign in'})

Title: Username is focused on load
Steps:
1. Go to /
2. Read document.activeElement
Expected Result: Username input holds focus without any click.

Title: Sign in is disabled until both fields have content
Steps:
1. Observe button
2. Type into Username only
3. Observe button
4. Type into Password
Expected Result: Disabled on load. Still disabled with only Username. Enabled once both have content.

Title: Password field masks input
Steps:
1. Type into Password
2. Read the type attribute
Expected Result: Input type is 'password'; the value is not rendered as readable text.

Title: Owner signs in and lands on Live Monitoring
Preconditions: Test realm seeded. User 'owner' exists with role owner
Steps:
1. Go to /
2. Fill Username
3. Fill Password
4. Click Sign in
5. Wait for the dashboard
Expected Result: Login form is replaced by the dashboard. 'Live Monitoring' heading visible. Sidebar with 7 items visible.

Title: Button shows a spinner and 'Signing in…' during submit
Preconditions: Signed out. Route /api/auth/login delayed ~1s via page.route
Steps:
1. Fill both fields
2. Click Sign in
3. Observe the button before the response lands
Expected Result: Button label reads 'Signing in…'. Button disabled. Both inputs disabled.

Title: Access token is not readable from JavaScript
Steps:
1. Sign in
2. Evaluate document.cookie
3. Read context.cookies()
Expected Result: document.cookie contains neither ww_access nor ww_refresh. context.cookies() shows both with httpOnly true.

Title: Reload keeps the user signed in
Steps:
1. Sign in
2. page.reload()
3. Wait for the dashboard
Expected Result: Dashboard renders directly. Login form never appears.

Title: Signed-out visit to any path shows Login
Steps:
1. Go to /
2. Confirm Login
3. Go to /?view=analytics
4. Confirm Login
Expected Result: Login form shown both times. No dashboard content is rendered behind it.

Title: Viewer signs in and reaches the dashboard
Preconditions: Test realm has a viewer user
Steps:
1. Sign in as the viewer
2. Wait for the dashboard
Expected Result: Dashboard renders. Sidebar visible.

Title: Admin signs in and reaches the dashboard
Preconditions: Test realm has an admin user
Steps:
1. Sign in as the admin
2. Wait for the dashboard
Expected Result: Dashboard renders. Sidebar visible.

Title: Enter submits the form
Steps:
1. Fill Username
2. Fill Password
3. Press Enter in the Password field
Expected Result: Form submits; dashboard renders. No mouse used.

Title: Error container carries role=alert
Steps:
1. Fill both fields
2. Submit
3. Read the alert region
Expected Result: An element with role='alert' is visible containing the failure message.

Title: Login is usable at 375px
Steps:
1. Set viewport
2. Go to /
3. Measure document scrollWidth
Expected Result: Both fields and the button are visible and tappable. scrollWidth <= 375, i.e. no horizontal scroll.

Title: Signing out returns to Login and ends the session
Steps:
1. Sign in
2. Open the bottom-left sidebar block
3. Click Sign out
4. Reload
Expected Result: Login form shown. Reload still shows Login, i.e. the session did not survive.

Title: Username and role show in the bottom-left sidebar
Steps:
1. Sign in
2. Read the bottom-left sidebar block
Expected Result: Username 'owner' and role 'owner' are visible above the clock.

Title: Dashboard opens on Live Monitoring
Steps:
1. Sign in
2. Read the page heading and the active nav item
Expected Result: Heading 'Live Monitoring'. The 'Live Monitoring' nav item has the active state.

Title: All seven navigation items are present
Steps: 1. Read sidebar item labels
Expected Result: Exactly these, in order: Live Monitoring, Camera Map, Analytics, Event History, Timeline Playback, Camera Management, Settings.

Title: Clicking 'Camera Map' switches the main panel
Preconditions: Signed in as owner, on Live Monitoring
Steps:
1. Click 'Camera Map' in the sidebar
2. Wait for the panel to change
Expected Result: The Camera Map view renders and its nav item shows the active state. Live Monitoring content is gone.

Title: Clicking 'Analytics' switches the main panel
Preconditions: Signed in as owner, on Live Monitoring
Steps:
1. Click 'Analytics' in the sidebar
2. Wait for the panel to change
Expected Result: The Analytics view renders and its nav item shows the active state. Live Monitoring content is gone.

Title: Clicking 'Event History' switches the main panel
Preconditions: Signed in as owner, on Live Monitoring
Steps:
1. Click 'Event History' in the sidebar
2. Wait for the panel to change
Expected Result: The Event History view renders and its nav item shows the active state. Live Monitoring content is gone.

Title: Clicking 'Timeline Playback' switches the main panel
Preconditions: Signed in as owner, on Live Monitoring
Steps:
1. Click 'Timeline Playback' in the sidebar
2. Wait for the panel to change
Expected Result: The Timeline Playback view renders and its nav item shows the active state. Live Monitoring content is gone.

Title: Clicking 'Camera Management' switches the main panel
Preconditions: Signed in as owner, on Live Monitoring
Steps:
1. Click 'Camera Management' in the sidebar
2. Wait for the panel to change
Expected Result: The Camera Management view renders and its nav item shows the active state. Live Monitoring content is gone.

Title: Clicking 'Settings' switches the main panel
Preconditions: Signed in as owner, on Live Monitoring
Steps:
1. Click 'Settings' in the sidebar
2. Wait for the panel to change
Expected Result: The Settings view renders and its nav item shows the active state. Live Monitoring content is gone.

Title: Navigating away and back restores Live Monitoring
Steps:
1. Click Analytics
2. Click Live Monitoring
3. Read the heading
Expected Result: Live Monitoring renders again with the camera grid.

Title: Grid renders one tile per camera
Preconditions: Signed in. Seed 3 cameras via the API before the test
Steps:
1. Sign in
2. Count camera tiles
Expected Result: Tile count equals the camera count from GET /api/cameras. Each tile shows its camera name.

Title: Changing grid layout changes visible tile count
Steps:
1. Note the default 3x3
2. Click the 2x2 layout control
3. Count tiles
Expected Result: Tile count changes to match the selected layout and the chosen control shows an active state.

Title: Sidebar clock shows 24-hour time and ticks
Steps:
1. Read the clock text
2. Wait 2s
3. Read it again
Expected Result: Matches /^\d{2}:\d{2}:\d{2}$/ with no AM/PM. The second reading differs from the first.

Title: Active alert count shows on the bell
Preconditions: Signed in. Seed 2 active alerts before the test
Steps:
1. Seed alerts
2. Reload
3. Read the badge
Expected Result: Badge reads '2'.

Title: Bell opens the alert panel
Preconditions: Signed in, at least 1 active alert
Steps:
1. Click the bell
2. Wait for the panel
Expected Result: Panel slides in and lists the active alerts.

Title: Panel closes from its close control
Steps:
1. Click the panel close control
2. Confirm it is gone
Expected Result: Panel is no longer visible and the page is interactive again.

Title: An alert row shows severity, camera and time
Preconditions: Signed in. Seed 1 critical alert on a known camera
Steps:
1. Open the alert panel
2. Read the first row
Expected Result: Row shows the alert title, the camera name and a 24-hour timestamp.

Title: Acknowledging removes an alert from the active list
Preconditions: Signed in as viewer. Seed 1 active alert
Steps:
1. Open the panel
2. Click Acknowledge on the row
3. Wait for the list to update
Expected Result: Row leaves the active list and the bell badge decrements by one.

Title: Clicking an alert focuses its camera
Preconditions: Signed in. Seed 1 alert on a known camera
Steps:
1. Open the panel
2. Click the alert body
3. Observe the grid
Expected Result: Panel closes and the grid focuses the alert's camera.

Title: 'View history' switches to Event History
Steps:
1. Click 'View history'
2. Read the heading
Expected Result: Event History renders and the panel closes.

Title: Alert sound toggles between ON and OFF
Steps:
1. Read the toggle state
2. Click 'Alert Sound'
3. Read it again
Expected Result: Indicator flips ON to OFF (or OFF to ON) and the new state persists across a view switch.

Title: A pinned camera sorts first
Preconditions: Signed in. Seed 3 cameras with the alphabetically last one pinned
Steps:
1. Seed
2. Reload
3. Read tile order
Expected Result: The pinned camera is the first tile despite its name.
Test Data: cameras A, B, C with C pinned

Title: An offline camera shows a placeholder, not a black tile
Preconditions: Signed in. Seed 1 camera with status offline
Steps:
1. Seed
2. Reload
3. Read that tile
Expected Result: Tile shows an explicit offline state with the camera name, not an empty black rectangle.

Title: An online camera tile plays video
Preconditions: Signed in. MediaMTX publishing a known path
Steps:
1. Wait up to 10s
2. Read the <video> element's readyState and currentTime twice, 2s apart
Expected Result: readyState >= 2 and currentTime advances between the two reads.

Title: A fresh install shows an add-camera CTA
Preconditions: Signed in as admin. Zero cameras
Steps:
1. Ensure no cameras
2. Reload
3. Read the grid area
Expected Result: An 'Add your first camera' CTA is visible and routes to Camera Management with the add dialog open.

Title: A viewer does not see admin-only navigation
Steps:
1. Sign in as viewer
2. Read sidebar item labels
Expected Result: Camera Management and Settings are absent or visibly disabled.

Title: Landing is usable at 375px
Steps:
1. Set viewport
2. Sign in
3. Measure scrollWidth and locate the nav
Expected Result: No horizontal scroll (scrollWidth <= 375). Navigation is reachable via a drawer. At most one video element plays.

Title: Landing is usable at 768px
Steps:
1. Set viewport
2. Sign in
3. Measure scrollWidth
Expected Result: No horizontal scroll. Grid reflows to a readable tile count.

Title: Losing a camera raises a dashboard alert
Steps:
1. Stop the publisher
2. Wait up to 60s
3. Read the tile and the alert panel
Expected Result: Tile shows offline and an alert appears without a manual reload.
